newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul stocks jump 3.53 pct to new record high.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul stocks jump 3.53 pct to new record high.

text.p: Istanbul's composite stock market index (IMKB-100) surged to an all-time high of 73,846.73 on Wednesday against the previous record of 73,531.8 on July 8.
The IMKB-100 rose 3.53 percent to 73,846.73 as selective buying fuelled activity towards the close in the afternoon session.
Brokers said a cash influx was seen as the main reason behind the steep rise.
"The demand was oriented at the shares which mostly effect the index," said Turgay Ozaner from Global securities.
The shares of utility firms and private Turkish Is Bank led the activity. Their traded volume reached 43 percent of the total.
Total daily volume rose to 12.16 trillion lira vs 7.89 trillion lira on Tuesday.
Brokers said that the upward movement might continue depending on the cash entry adding the index targeted 79,000-80,000 levels in short-term.
"The index should follow dollar's rise. It was meaningless for the index to be steady stay while the dollar goes up," said Hakan Demirbulak from Tatbank securities.
He also said the index would not find strong barriers to reach 75,000.
Out of the 224 shares traded, 153 rose, 44 were steady and 27 declined.
Financial index ended 3.4 percent up at 65,435.66, industrial index went 3.58 percent up to 81,004.89.
